title: Variant Parity Inspector — visualizer and rollback guard
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: When teams run A/B or canary rollouts we surface metrics, logs and traffic splits, but it's still hard for product owners and SREs to quickly determine if behavioral regressions exist across variants. This ticket proposes a Variant Parity Inspector: a compact visualizer that compares outputs from active variants side-by-side, highlights semantic and token-level diffs, and synthesizes a rollback risk score to help rapid human decisions.

Goals:
- Provide a single-pane comparison for sample requests (text/chat/structured outputs) across up to 3 concurrent variants.
- Visualize differences at multiple granularities: intent/label mismatch, response length, token-level edit highlights, and probability-similarity heatmap.
- Surface telemetry signals (latency, error rate, rate of hallucination) aggregated by variant and correlated to the specific sample.
- Offer contextual rollback affordances (pin sample to rollout, add as regression exemplar, quick rollback button with pre-populated reason).

User stories:
- As a PM, I want to preview candidate model outputs for key prompts to confirm parity before increasing traffic.
- As an SRE, I want a signal that correlates latency spikes with particular variants for rapid mitigation.
- As a data scientist, I want an easy way to mark failing samples and export them to the eval suite.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Prototype UI shows side-by-side output panes, diff overlay, and a small panel with aggregated telemetry for the selected sample.
2) Prototype includes a lightweight rollback guard: clicking rollback opens a confirmation with suggested reasons and links to open a change request (PM/ENG).
3) Design handoff includes annotated components, accessibility notes (contrast, keyboard nav), and a developer interaction spec for telemetry hooks.

Success metrics:
- Time to decision reduced by 30% in internal trials when using the inspector vs. metrics-only workflow.
- Number of false-positive rollbacks reduced by 20% after using parity highlights.

Assumptions and constraints:
- Backend will supply side-by-side outputs and per-token alignment scores (ENG-7821). If not available, fallback to text-diff with per-response metadata.
- Prototype uses sampled traffic and synthetic prompts; must include privacy checklist for PII handling.
- Initially supports up to 3 variants to keep UI manageable.
